elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained opener: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT ... EXCEED" — the cap binds both Corio (Customer) and Commerce One (Vendor).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: As redlined the cap is "THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION" — no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor and "actually paid" only, not "paid or payable".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Second sentence retained: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS ... OR FOR ANY INDIRECT, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "AND EXCEPT FOR EITHER PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS ..." placed in the cap sentence's exception opener, so such liability sits outside the cap for both parties.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The inserted carve-out list names only confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears in Section 9.

Retained "EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT"; Section 8 (p0086, "8.1 By Commerce One. Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless...") is the indemnification section.
Inserted exception expressly covers "EITHER PARTY'S ... GROSS NEGLIGENCE".
Inserted exception expressly covers "... OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" for either party.
No fraud carve-out anywhere in the rendered Section 9; the exception list stops at willful misconduct.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Only "LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8" (the indemnity) is excepted; a direct claim for infringement of the other party's IP outside the Section 8 indemnity remains capped.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: The cap covers "EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT" with no statement that Corio's obligation to pay fees is not "damages" subject to the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ... EXCEED" — mutual as originally drafted and unchanged.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Deletion of "FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO" leaves "THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION" — a genuine 12-months-of-fees basis; fallback does not require "paid or payable".
"EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT" carves the indemnification section out of the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Inserted "EXCEPT FOR EITHER PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS" in the cap sentence.
Inserted exception includes "GROSS NEGLIGENCE" for either party.
Inserted exception includes "WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" for either party.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the cap is mutual and, after deleting the per-transaction narrowing, is measured by all amounts actually paid by Corio in the 12 months before the cause of action; indemnification (Section 8) was already outside the cap and confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct are now expressly carved out in operative language, not merely promised in the comment.

Preferred is not reached: no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid" rather than "paid or payable", and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud, or infringement of the other party's IP (the Section 8 exception covers only indemnity liability), and no statement that Corio's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. These are acceptable gaps at the fallback level but should be named in the rationale if preferred is pressed.

Minimality holds: only two edits were made — deleting the transaction-slice qualifier (necessary to convert the basis to 12 months of fees) and extending the existing exception opener with the three missing carve-outs. No survival tails, procedures, damages categories or other extras were added, and the favourable mutual consequential-damages sentence and the "reasonable allocation of risk" sentence were left intact.

Intent preserved: the exception structure, the Section 8 cross-reference, the filing-of-cause-of-action temporal anchor and the mutual exclusion sentence all survive without contradiction; no defined term is left dangling.

Classification as "deviation" is correct — before the edit the cap was a per-transaction slice that could fall below six months' fees (walk-away territory) and confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct were inside the cap.
